c: Gatti Amari summons cats from a hexagram on the edge of the screen. These cats mostly walk around in a straight line and may change direction after a while, and have a chance to attack with their claws when they are close to the enemies. They can also occasionally hurt the player character when they are close to it, dealing twice the usual damage. When a cat is close to another, they have a chance to start a fight, which creates a huge Area-of-Effect of cartoonish scuffle cloud that lasts for a while. If a cat walks over a Pickup on the screen, it gets automatically consumed, affecting the cat in different ways.
affects both how big the claw attacks and the scuffle are.
affects how long the cats remain on the screen as well as how long the scuffle lasts.

Gatti Amari's scratches have a 1 second Hitbox Delay and its scuffle has a 0.03 seconds Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every second and 0.03 seconds respectively. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often. This does not apply to claw attacks as they do not last long enough to hit twice.
Pickups consumed by the cats have varying effects on them:
Floor Chicken permanently increases the chance stat and Base Damage.
explodes the cat that consumed it.
The explosion is the same as from
Gilded Clover make the cat that consumes them run twice as fast.
Orologion freezes the cat that consumed it. It can be used by the player instead.
Vacuum have no additional effects. It can be used by the player instead.
The chance for most interactions of the cats is affected by
, multiplying the chance stat of the weapon.
Increases the chance for the cats to attack enemies.
Decreases the chance for the cats to attack the player.
Increases the chance for them to start a scuffle.
Increases the chance of Pickups that are not beneficial to the cats being used by the player instead.

When level up options contain Gatti Amari, instead of raining
Experience Gems, it rains cats. It is probably a reference to the saying "raining cats and dogs".
"Gatti Amari" is Italian for "bitter cats", although it resembles the expression "cazzi amari" ("bitter dicks") which colloquially means "shit gets real".
